keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the research should cover only scheduling features or also messaging, expense tracking, document storage, etc. changes which apps qualify and how deeply each is evaluated.
Whether this is for two parents only, involves grandparents or other caregivers, or multiple households affects which app's sharing and permission features matter most.
The current custody arrangement (e.g., 50/50, primary/secondary, long-distance) shapes which scheduling features are most critical to research for.
A hard budget limit (free-only vs. paid) significantly narrows the candidate app list and changes the comparison criteria.
Whether the priority is simplicity/ease of use, legal documentation features, or conflict-minimizing communication tools changes which apps to highlight in the research.
Knowing the end deliverable — a personal shortlist, a side-by-side comparison, a recommendation to share with the other parent — defines how thorough and formatted the output needs to be.
Knowing which devices or platforms both parents use (iOS, Android, web) is a hard filter that can immediately eliminate incompatible apps from consideration.

gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate co-parenting apps that help with child scheduling between two parents or households.

questions.title: Which features matter beyond scheduling, like messaging or expenses?
questions.description: Determine whether the research scope is limited to calendar/scheduling tools or should also cover communication, expense splitting, document storage, and other co-parenting features.

questions.title: How many people need access to the app?
questions.description: Clarify whether access is just for two parents, or also needs to include grandparents, step-parents, teachers, or other caregivers.

questions.title: What does your current custody schedule look like?
questions.description: Understand the custody arrangement (e.g., 50/50, primary/secondary, long-distance) to identify which scheduling capabilities are most critical.

questions.title: Are you open to paid apps, or is free a hard requirement?
questions.description: Establish budget constraints to immediately filter out apps that fall outside the acceptable price range.

questions.title: What is your top priority — simplicity, legal records, or low conflict?
questions.description: Identify which value matters most to the user to determine which app strengths to emphasize in the research.

questions.title: What does a useful end result look like to you?
questions.description: Determine whether the goal is a personal shortlist, a detailed comparison chart, or a recommendation ready to share with the other parent.

questions.title: What devices or platforms do both parents use?
questions.description: Identify iOS, Android, or web requirements for both users to filter out incompatible apps from the start.
